subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome MCP existing-session `profile=user` reports ready but all page tools time out on macOS

question: Should OpenClaw continue treating Chrome MCP auto-connect `profile=user` as a supported signed-in browser path, or steer affected users to the restored extension driver or explicit `cdpUrl` endpoint path?
rationale: Current source and related PRs show partial readiness diagnostics but not a root fix, and the remaining choice depends on maintainer support boundaries for Chrome permission-gated debugging versus the newer extension/CDP alternatives.

options.title: Trace and fix Chrome MCP
options.body: Capture a live macOS Chrome trace for `status`, `tabs`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, and `evaluate`, then repair or diagnose the Chrome MCP path from that evidence.

options.title: Document unsupported state
options.body: If the trace shows an upstream Chrome/Chrome DevTools MCP limitation, document the exact failure mode and fast actionable fallback instead of trying wrapper retries.

options.title: Route to extension/CDP endpoint
options.body: Treat signed-in Chrome automation as owned by the extension driver or explicit endpoint profiles and close this only after docs and CLI messaging make that boundary clear.

recommendation.title: Trace and fix Chrome MCP
recommendation.body: Capture a live macOS Chrome trace for `status`, `tabs`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, and `evaluate`, then repair or diagnose the Chrome MCP path from that evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the current assignee and recently owned the browser extension relay and status follow-up work that frame the support-boundary choice.
